text: Should public money help pay for election campaigns?
That is the question behind California Proposition four.
Proposition four would let more governments offer public
financing.
It does not automatically launch a program or
send money to candidates.
Candidates would have to demonstrate broad support in
their district and accept spending limits.
But other public funds spent on campaigns still
have an opportunity cost.
A voter favoring reform might say:
I want candidates with community support to compete,
even without wealthy backers.
Another voter might ask: should taxpayers pay for
political campaigns?
They may dislike funding candidates they oppose, or
prefer other uses for public money.
A no vote keeps the general ban and
existing exceptions.
